title: Binder Transactions, Proxies, Stubs, Identity, and Death Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies binder transactions, proxies, stubs, identity, and death?
options: Treat Binder as bounded remote execution with kernel identity, scheduling, failure, reentrancy, and versioned contract concerns.
questions.answer: Treat Binder as bounded remote execution with kernel identity, scheduling, failure, reentrancy, and versioned contract concerns.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: A one-way Binder transaction cannot be delayed by a busy remote process.
questions.explanation: Holding a mutex while making a synchronous Binder call can deadlock when the remote service calls back into code that needs the same mutex.

questions.prompt: Why must authorization happen before clearCallingIdentity?
questions.answer: The original kernel-supplied caller identity is the trustworthy subject; clearing it changes subsequent checks to the service identity.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
